clue.text: Less than lashings of entertainment here?

definitions.text: Less than lashings of entertainment here?

parts.words: Less than lashings of entertainment here
parts.note: small light strokes of a whip are less than full lashings, and the same word is slang for the cinema, a place of entertainment

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a show offers less than plenty of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lashings' looks like British slang for 'lots'; read it as whip strokes, and small ones are the light cracks that also name the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the cinema or the films shown there; also small quick strokes, less than a full lash.

clue.text: Permission to go

parts.note: an official grant allowing someone to be absent, such as a soldier's furlough

explanation.definitionFit: Granting someone time away from duty is giving them formal permission to be absent.

clue.text: Unlike the scatterbrain

parts.note: a scatterbrain is flustered and disorganised; the opposite is calm and composed, as if gathered together

explanation.definitionFit: Composed and self-possessed, the reverse of a scatterbrain whose thoughts are strewn everywhere.

clue.text: There's no putting straight will solve this problem

definitions.text: There's no putting straight will solve this problem

parts.words: There's no putting straight will solve this problem
parts.note: in old golf rules, a ball blocking the line between another ball and the hole could not be putted past directly

explanation.surface: A tangle so bad that no amount of setting things right will fix it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting straight' sounds like tidying up; in golf it is putting the ball straight at the hole, which an opponent's ball in the way prevents.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf obstruction, an opposing ball in the putting line, extended to mean any thwarting predicament.

clue.text: A double helping of meat, double quick !

indicators.note: a double helping means the cut of meat is served up twice in succession

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: A diner orders two portions of meat and wants it served fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A double helping of' says to write CHOP twice.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation urging speed, meaning hurry up, at once.

clue.text: The nebulous world of wandering wits-or voices?

definitions.text: The nebulous world of wandering wits-or voices?

parts.words: The nebulous world of wandering wits-or voices
parts.note: a fanciful dream realm up among the clouds, for those whose wits wander, or for the bird whose call is its own name

explanation.surface: A vague imaginary place where minds drift and voices are heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The realm comes from Aristophanes' Birds: 'nebulous' points to clouds, 'wandering wits' to being crazy, and 'voices' to the bird named for its two-note call.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealised fantasy realm of impractical dreamers, originally the birds' city in the sky in Aristophanes.

clue.text: A balmy sort of fly-trap?

parts.note: a soothing salve, the thing in which the proverbial fly spoils everything

explanation.surface: A gentle device for catching flies.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'a fly in the' salve means one small flaw; the salve is pictured as having trapped the fly, and 'balmy' means like a balm.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing salve or balm, famous from the idiom of a fly spoiling it.

clue.text: Acted very strangely for a trainee

indicators.note: the word acted is behaving very strangely, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in training behaved very oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very strangely' turns ACTED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A young person training for the armed forces or police is a trainee officer.

clue.text: Like the alfresco feast ?

parts.note: a meal laid out in the open air is a spread set out of doors, and the word also means stretched wide

explanation.surface: Describing a picnic laid out in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as 'out' plus 'spread': a feast set out of doors is a spread laid outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Extended wide open, as a picnic spread is laid out in the open.

clue.text: John the Grain

parts.note: the folk personification of malt liquor and the cereal crop is given the first name John

explanation.definitionFit: John Barleycorn is the folk-song figure personifying the cereal and the beer and whisky made from it.

clue.text: Fruit that changes daily

definitions.meaning: the sweet brown fruit of a palm tree
the day of the month, which moves on every day

explanation.surface: A fruit whose nature alters every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the palm's sweet fruit and the calendar day, which advances every twenty-four hours.

clue.text: A prophet's tale of woe

parts.note: a long mournful complaint, named after the Old Testament prophet of Lamentations

explanation.definitionFit: A long lament, named after the prophet Jeremiah, traditional author of Lamentations.

clue.text: Architectural feature drives me to drink

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily

explanation.surface: Some building detail is so maddening it makes the speaker turn to the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drives me to drink' looks like an idiom; read 'drives' and 'to' as links, ME followed by TOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: In a Doric frieze, the square panel between triglyphs is a classical architectural element.

clue.text: A spree that leaves one broke ?

definitions.meaning: a bout of wild drinking or revelry

explanation.surface: A wild night out that empties the wallet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a riotous spree and the state of being penniless.

clue.text: Single-minded girl has the intelligence to embrace one thousand

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: one word holding the others in its arms, so they go inside it

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A determined young woman is clever enough to take on a thousand people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts I and M inside NOUS, giving NIMOUS after UNA; 'has the' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Of one mind: everyone agreeing completely, sharing a single opinion.

clue.text: Even run in distress to a copper' when frightened

indicators.note: the words even run are in a distressed state, so their letters are shaken up

parts.note: d stood for a penny, a copper coin in old British money

explanation.surface: A steady run in trouble, adding a policeman, when someone is scared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' turns EVEN RUN into UNNERVE; D is the old British penny, a copper coin, not a policeman. 'when frightened' defines a past participle used adjectivally.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaken and lacking nerve, as someone frightened is.

clue.text: Though formidable appeared to have fresh misgivings

definitions.meaning: split as re- plus doubted: doubted again

explanation.surface: Someone imposing seemed to doubt again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Though' is a link. The second definition splits the word as RE (again) plus DOUBTED.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for dreaded or feared, and read in parts, doubted once more.

clue.text: It's continuously being saved nowadays

parts.note: summer clock changes to make the most of the hours of sunlight are called a saving scheme

explanation.surface: Something that is being conserved all the time today.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1960s Britain clocks were kept an hour ahead all year (British Standard Time), so the sunlight was saved continuously.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunlight hours, preserved by putting clocks forward under the saving-time scheme.

clue.text: A difficult manoeuvre for the hungry sailor ?

definitions.text: A difficult manoeuvre for the hungry sailor ?

parts.words: A difficult manoeuvre for the hungry sailor
parts.note: a tough change of course under sail, read as tough ship's biscuit eaten at sea

explanation.surface: A tricky bit of sailing for a seaman who wants his dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: HARD (difficult) plus TACK (a change of course under sail) is also the hard ship's biscuit a hungry sailor ate.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard ship's biscuit, the staple ration of sailors on long voyages.

clue.text: The same again and again for this bird

indicators.note: repeating the word for the same means writing it twice

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same

explanation.surface: A bird that keeps saying the same thing over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' is the old abbreviation for ditto, the same; 'again and again' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct flightless bird of Mauritius.

clue.text: A drinking bout with the Arabs ? How beastly !

definitions.note: the exclamation is a hint that the answer is a beast, so it is noun against exclamation

parts.note: a jag is a spell of heavy drinking
UAR is the United Arab Republic, the union of Egypt and Syria

explanation.surface: Someone appalled by a boozing session with Arab companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. UAR is the United Arab Republic of 1958-71; the definition is the exclamation 'How beastly!' pointing to an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A big spotted cat of the Americas, a true beast.

clue.text: Ancient firearm

definitions.meaning: an ancient is an old word for an ensign, the rank of Shakespeare's swaggerer ... in Henry IV and Henry V

explanation.surface: An old gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' looks like an adjective for 'firearm'; it is the old military rank, as in Ancient Pistol of Shakespeare's history plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Ancient (ensign) Pistol, and a handgun.

clue.text: It's in the barn

parts.note: the great medieval barns that stored the tenth of produce owed to the church carry this name

explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of produce paid to the church, stored in a so-called tithe barn.

clue.text: Pythian for instance

parts.note: the Pythia was Apollo's priestess at Delphi, who spoke prophecies

explanation.definitionFit: Of an oracle; Pythian refers to the Delphic priestess who delivered prophecies.

clue.text: Blue heaven

explanation.definitionFit: A clear sky-blue colour, and in poetry the cloudless sky itself.

clue.text: Runaway ex-blue ?

definitions.meaning: to make a sudden dash for it, as a horse does
something that comes out of the blue, as in a thunderbolt from a clear sky

explanation.surface: A fugitive who used to be a sky colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ex-blue' is 'out of the blue', as in a bolt from the blue; 'Runaway' is a sudden escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden dash away, and the thunderbolt proverbially arriving from a clear sky.

clue.text: Take it out, sugar — anyway it's free

indicators.note: the letters are to be taken in any way at all, so they get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told to remove an item and assured it costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' scrambles IT OUT and SUGAR; 'Take' and 'it's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Given without charge or reason, provided for nothing.

clue.text: Made Bill act royally

parts.note: a parliamentary bill becomes law once the monarch formally agrees to it

explanation.surface: Someone got a man named Bill to behave like a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is a draft law, which becomes an Act when the monarch gives Royal consent.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed; the monarch's formal agreement turns a bill into an Act of Parliament.

clue.text: Of course it makes a difference

definitions.text: Of course it makes a difference

parts.words: Of course it makes a difference
parts.note: the steering blade at the stern changes the vessel's course

explanation.surface: Naturally, it matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like 'naturally'; read it as the ship's heading, which this part alters.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinged blade at a ship's stern that steers it, changing its heading.
